chunks: I asked al-Reza (peace be upon him) about tawhid (Divine Unity), so he said: 'Whoever recites "Say: He is God, the One" and believes in it, has indeed recognized tawhid.' I said: 'How should one recite it?' He said: 'Just as the people recite it, and add to it: "Thus is God, my Lord; thus is God, my Lord."'

key_terms.التوحيد: Tawhid — the doctrine of Divine Unity or Oneness; the foundational theological concept in Islam
key_terms.عَرَفَ: Recognized/knew — not merely intellectual acknowledgment but deep spiritual recognition (ma'rifa)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Surah al-Ikhlas 112:1 — 'Say: He is God, the One'; this surah is considered equivalent to one-third of the Quran
key_terms.كَذَلِكَ اللَّهُ رَبِّي: Thus is God, my Lord — an additional affirmation prescribed by the Imam as a devotional supplement to the surah

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Reza say about recognizing tawhid through Surah al-Ikhlas?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi asks Imam al-Reza (AS) about tawhid and receives a profound yet accessible answer: reciting Surah al-Ikhlas (112:1) with genuine belief is itself recognition of Divine Unity. The Imam further instructs that after the standard recitation, one should add the personal affirmation 'Thus is God, my Lord' twice — a devotional formula that personalizes the abstract doctrine of tawhid. This teaching reflects the Shia tradition of making theological concepts accessible through acts of worship.
